source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)

verses.translation: And it happened when he entered into the house of one of the leaders [or: chiefs] of the Pharisees to eat bread [or: food] on the Sabbath, and behold they were watching him [closely]

translation_notes: בבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 (same), H1006 'Bajith (place name)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because the context describes entering a physical dwelling for a meal.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because it functions as a numeral modifying 'rulers' — one of the rulers.

משר (consonants שר): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/ruler', H8270 'a string/cord'. Chose H8269 because the passage describes a social setting — entering the house of a prominent person among the Pharisees.
פת: Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel (of bread)', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 because the context is eating — 'to eat bread/a morsel' is a standard Hebrew idiom for dining.

והנם: The only Strong's candidate is H2011 'Hinnom (a Jebusite name)' which makes no sense here. This is clearly a pronominal form וְהֵנָּם / וְהִנָּם meaning 'and they/and behold they,' a common Mishnaic Hebrew demonstrative pronoun not well represented in Strong's. Translated as 'and they [were].'
textual_notes: ונעשת — This form does not appear in Strong's candidates. It appears to be a Mishnaic/late Hebrew form meaning 'and it happened/came to pass,' possibly from עשה in a reflexive stem or a variant of ויהי. No Strong's number assigned.
כשנכנס — A compound form (כש + נכנס) meaning 'when he entered,' using the late Hebrew verb נכנס. No Strong's candidates provided.
הפרושים — 'the Pharisees' — a post-biblical term for the sect, derived from פרש (to separate). No Strong's candidates given.
ב&בת — Appears to be בשבת 'on the Sabbath' with the shin corrupted or marked. The ampersand likely indicates a damaged or uncertain letter.
והנם — The Strong's candidate H2011 (Hinnom) is clearly wrong for this context. This must be a pronominal/demonstrative form.

verses.literal: And it happened when he entered into [the] house [of] one [of the] rulers [of] the Pharisees to eat bread on [the] Sabbath and they [were] watching him

verses.translation: And behold, a certain man [who was] swollen [with dropsy] was before him

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because this is a narrative introduction drawing attention to a new character — 'and behold' fits perfectly.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act manly'. Chose H376 because a noun is needed as the subject of the clause.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one man' meaning 'a certain man.'
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because the context requires a copula — the man 'was' before him.
textual_notes: משוקה — No Strong's candidates provided. The consonants שקה relate to drinking/watering (H8248 שקה 'to give drink') but in a passive/nominal form could indicate being 'waterlogged' or swollen, i.e., suffering from dropsy (edema). This is consistent with the Mishnaic Hebrew medical term. The root could also relate to שוק (H7785 'leg/thigh') but 'swollen with fluid' fits the narrative better, as the passage sets up a healing scenario.
לפניו — Compound form: ל + פני + ו = 'before him / to his face.' פנים (H6440) with preposition and suffix. No ambiguity in meaning.

verses.literal: And behold a man one swollen he was before him

verses.translation: And Yeshua [Joshua/Jesus] responded and said to the experts [or: sages] of the law and the Pharisees: Is it permitted [or: fitting, proper] to perform healing on the Sabbath?

translation_notes: וישוע: Candidates: H3442 and H3443, both 'Jeshua/Yeshua.' Chose H3442 as the standard entry for this proper name.

ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to heed/respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 (Aramaic 'respond'), H6033 (Aramaic 'depress'), H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because 'answered and said' is the classic Hebrew narrative formula for responding in speech.

ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 (Aramaic 'to say'), H561 'something said', H562 (same), H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' following 'answered' is the standard Hebrew speech formula.
הדת: Candidates: H1881 'a royal edict/statute/law', H1882 (same, Aramaic). Chose H1881 because 'wise ones of the law' describes Torah scholars, the standard designation for legal experts.
textual_notes: לחכמי — No Strong's candidates given. From חכם (H2450 'wise') in construct plural with ל preposition: 'to the wise ones of.' This is a term for Torah scholars/legal experts, equivalent to 'lawyers' or 'scribes' in other traditions.

לעשות — The candidates H6219 'shining/polished' and H6220 'Ashvath (name)' do not fit. This is clearly the infinitive construct of עשה (H6213 'to do/make') with ל preposition, a standard Hebrew construction meaning 'to do/perform.' The provided Strong's candidates match different consonantal roots.

הראוי — No Strong's candidates provided. This appears to be from ראה (to see) in a passive participial form meaning 'seen as fitting/proper/permitted' — a standard Mishnaic Hebrew term for legal permissibility.
רפואה — No Strong's candidates provided. From רפא (H7495 'to heal') — the noun form meaning 'healing/remedy/cure.'
ב&בת — Same as section 1, likely בשבת 'on the Sabbath' with damaged/marked shin.

verses.literal: And Yeshua answered and said to [the] wise ones [of] the law and the Pharisees [is it] fitting to do healing on [the] Sabbath

verses.translation: And they were silent and he healed the man and released him
words: and released him / let him go

translation_notes: והוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/self', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because 'and he healed' requires the personal pronoun.

האדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. Chose H120 because 'the man' (the sick person just described) is the coherent referent of healing.
textual_notes: ועזבו could mean 'and he left him' or 'and he released/sent him away'. Both are plausible from the root עזב (to leave/forsake/release). In a healing context, 'released him' or 'let him go' is the more natural reading.

verses.literal: And they were silent and he healed the man and released him

verses.translation: And he answered to them and said which [one] of you if his ox and his donkey falling in [a] pit on [the] Sabbath that not he will pull it up

translation_notes: וענה (consonants ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to answer', H6031 'to afflict'. Chose H6030 as the dialogue continuation.
להם: ל + הם. Chose H1992 'them' as the prepositional object.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559.

אי (consonants אי): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 because 'which' (interrogative) paired with זה = 'which one' makes sense in a rhetorical question.
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה = 'which one' is a standard interrogative construction.
אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'a mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'if his ox falls' is the conditional clause.
בבור (consonants בור): Candidates: H952 'to bore/examine', H953 'a pit/cistern'. Chose H953 because 'falling into a pit' is the coherent physical image.
textual_notes: שורו: The provided candidate for רו is H7299 'aspect', which does not fit. The consonants שור clearly point to 'ox' (from שור, an ox/bull), with the possessive suffix ו. This is a standard Hebrew word not adequately covered by the candidate list.

The phrase שלא יעלהו could be parsed as 'that not he-will-raise-it' (rhetorical question expecting the answer 'of course he would') or as a statement. The rhetorical question reading is more coherent.

verses.literal: And he answered to them and said which [one] of you if his ox and his donkey falling in [a] pit on [the] Sabbath that not he will pull it up

verses.translation: And not they were able to answer him

translation_notes: ולא (consonants לא): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 same. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.

לענות: The provided candidate H6039 'affliction' (noun) does not fit the infinitive construct context. This is ל + ענות, the infinitive of ענה (H6030 'to answer'). The ל prefix marks purpose/infinitive: 'to answer'.
textual_notes: לענות could theoretically derive from H6031 'to afflict' (infinitive: 'to afflict him') but context of a debate clearly favors 'to answer him' from H6030.

verses.literal: And not they were able to answer him

verses.translation: And he said to those the invited [ones] a word a parable when they chose seats the first and [a] seat [of] honor

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559.

דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'a pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'a word/matter' = a teaching/parable fits the context of telling a story to guests.
כאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 with כ prefix = 'as/when', because 'when they chose' introduces the observed action.
מושבות: The candidate H7622 'exile/captivity' does not fit. The consonants מושבות point to the plural of מושב (a seat/dwelling, from ישב 'to sit'). Context of a banquet clearly favors 'seats'.
וכסא (consonants כסא): Candidates: H3677 'full moon/festival', H3678 'throne/seat'. Chose H3678 because 'seat of honor' at a banquet is the coherent image.
textual_notes: נשמע is ambiguous: it could be a niphal participle of שמע 'to hear' (meaning 'heard' or 'a thing heard', i.e. a parable/teaching), or it could be parsed differently. In this context it seems to function as a descriptor of דבר — 'a word heard' meaning a parable or teaching.
דבר נשמע together could mean 'a parable' (literally 'a word/matter [to be] heard') or could be two separate clauses. The parable reading fits since what follows is clearly a teaching story.

verses.literal: And he said to those the invited [ones] a word a parable when they chose seats the first and [a] seat [of] honor

verses.translation: When they will call you to [a] wedding do not sit at [the] head for perhaps more honored than you [has been] called there

translation_notes: אשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 as the conjunction 'when' paired with כ.
אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect תשב = 'do not sit', the standard prohibitive construction.

בראש (consonants ראש): Candidates: H7217 'head/sum', H7218 'head (most applications)', H7219 'poison plant', H7220 'Rosh'. Chose H7218 because 'at the head [place]' of a banquet table is the coherent image.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction.
באולי: Candidates: H194 'perhaps', H195 'Ulai river', H196 'foolish/impious'. Chose H194 because 'perhaps someone more honored' is the natural reasoning in a banquet context.
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'a name/honor', H8035 'Shem'. Chose H8033 'there' because 'has been called there' = invited to that same seat.

verses.literal: When they will call you to [a] wedding do not sit at [the] head for perhaps more honored than you [has been] called there

verses.translation: And he will come the one who invited you and he will say to you give place to this [one] and then in shame you will go down lower lower

translation_notes: תן: The candidate H8565 'a sea-serpent/jackal' does not fit. This is the imperative of נתן 'to give'. Context demands 'give [your] place'.
מקום (consonants מקום/קום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing spot', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because 'give place' = yield your spot.
לזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'to this one' = to this person.
ואז: H227 'then/therefore'. Straightforward temporal conjunction.

מטה (first, consonants מטה): Candidates: H4294 'a branch/rod/tribe', H4295 'downward/below', H4296 'a bed', H4297 'distortion', H4298 'expansion'. Chose H4295 because 'you will go down lower' is the coherent image of descending to a lower seat.
מטה (second): Same candidates. Chose H4295 again. The repetition מטה מטה emphasizes 'lower and lower' or 'to the very lowest place'.
textual_notes: שזמנך contains the root זמן (to appoint/invite) with a relative prefix ש and 2ms suffix ך — 'the one who invited you'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew construction.
תן is clearly the imperative of נתן despite the candidate H8565 being unrelated.

verses.literal: And he will come the one who invited you and he will say to you give place to this [one] and then in shame you will go down lower lower

verses.translation: But when you are called go [for yourself] and sit in [the] place the most last in rank so that when he comes the one who invited you he will say to you beloved come up here then you will gain elevation before the invited [ones]

translation_notes: רק (consonants רק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'but/rather' introduces the contrasting instruction after the negative example.
כאשר: Chose H834 'when' with כ prefix, same as previous sections.
במקום: Candidates: H4725 'a place', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 'in the place'.
היותר: H3148 'more/most'. The ה prefix makes it superlative: 'the most'.
אחרון: H314 'last/hinder/western'. 'The most last' = the lowest/last place.

במעלה (consonants מעלה/עלה): Candidates: H4608 'elevation/platform', H4609 'elevation/rank/ascent', H5927 'to ascend'. Chose H4609 because 'in rank/elevation' qualifies 'the most last' — the lowest in rank.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 as the purpose conjunction.

עלה (consonants עלה): Candidates: H5927 'to ascend', H5928 'a holocaust', H5929 'a leaf', H5930 'a step/stairs', H5931 'a pretext'. Chose H5927 because 'come up!' is the imperative invitation to ascend to a higher seat.
הנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/here', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2008 because 'come up here/hither' is the directional adverb matching the invitation.
מעלה (second instance): Candidates: H4608 'elevation', H4609 'elevation/rank'. Chose H4609 because 'you will gain elevation/honor' before the guests is the culminating reward image.
לפני: H3942 'anterior/before'. Straightforward prepositional usage.
textual_notes: שכשיבוא is a compound: ש + כש + יבוא ('that when he comes'). This is a post-biblical Hebrew construction using multiple relative/temporal particles.
אהוב could be parsed as a passive participle 'beloved/loved one' or as an adjective used as a term of address 'friend/dear one'. Both yield essentially the same meaning in this context.
במעלה in both occurrences could be H4608 or H4609; both mean 'elevation'. H4609 is chosen for both as it better captures the figurative sense of rank/status in a banquet setting.

verses.literal: But when you are called go [for yourself] and sit in [the] place the most last in rank so that when he comes the one who invited you he will say to you beloved come up here then you will gain elevation before the invited [ones]

verses.translation: For the one who elevates himself comes to lowliness and the one who lowers himself to be exalted.
words: the one who elevates (hiphil participle of גבה)
to the hands of / into the state of
the one who lowers (hiphil participle of שפל)
to be exalted (hitpael infinitive of נשא)

translation_notes: כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'conjunction: for, because, that'. Chose H3588 because the word introduces a causal or explanatory clause linking the two halves of the saying.
שפלות (consonants שפלות): Only candidate H8220 'remissness/lowliness'. Fits the context of being brought low as a consequence of self-exaltation.
textual_notes: להתנשאות: The hitpael infinitive construct of נשא could mean 'to exalt oneself' or 'to be exalted.' In this antithetical parallelism (the one who lowers himself → exaltation), the passive sense 'to be exalted' fits best as the reward for humility.

verses.literal: For the one who elevates himself comes to lowliness and the one who lowers himself to be exalted.

verses.translation: And he said to the one who called him when you make a meal of morning or a meal of evening do not desire to invite your lovers and not the brothers and not the relatives and not the wealthy neighbors for perhaps them that you [are] calling that they repay to you recompense.
words: desire/wish (from רצה, to be pleased, to desire)
to invite / to fix a time
your lovers / your friends (participle of אהב + 2ms suffix)

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates include H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a speech-introduction verb ('and he said').

לאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 as the relative pronoun 'to the one who' — it introduces the person who invited him.
בקר (consonants בקר): Candidates: H1239 'to plough/inspect', H1241 'cattle', H1242 'morning'. Chose H1242 'morning' because it pairs with ערב 'evening' to describe two types of meals.

ערב (consonants ערב): Candidates: H6148 'to intermix/traffic', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6153 'dusk/evening'. Chose H6153 'evening' as it pairs with בקר 'morning' for morning meal vs. evening meal.
אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 as the negative particle with the imperfect תרצה — 'do not desire.'

תרצה: The candidates list H8656 (Tirtsah, a place name). However, the consonants ת-ר-צ-ה clearly match the verb רצה (H7521, 'to desire/be pleased') in 2ms imperfect form. The place name Tirtsah does not fit a verbal context following אל. Chose to read as verb form of רצה.

באולי (consonants אולי): Candidates: H194 'perhaps', H195 'Ulai river', H196 'foolish/impious'. Chose H194 'perhaps' with prefix ב — the clause warns against inviting those who might reciprocate, making it a transactional exchange.
שאתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you (pronoun)'. Chose H859 — 'that you' as the subject of 'are calling.'

גמול (consonants גמול): Candidates: H1576 'recompense/requital', H1577 'Gamul (name)'. Chose H1576 — the sentence warns against inviting people who will repay you, i.e., making hospitality transactional.
ה<כנים: The damaged letter < likely represents שׁ, yielding השכנים 'the neighbors' (from H7934 שכן). This fits the list of people not to invite: friends, brothers, relatives, wealthy neighbors.
textual_notes: תרצה: The only Strong's candidate provided is H8656 (Tirtsah, a place name), but the grammatical context requires a 2ms imperfect verb. The consonants match רצה (H7521) perfectly. This is almost certainly the verb 'to desire/wish.'

ה<כנים: The damaged letter makes this word uncertain. Reading as השכנים (neighbors) fits the context of a list of social contacts. Alternatively, it could be a form of הכנים (those prepared/established).
קורא: The only candidate given is H6981 (Kore, a proper name), but the context demands a participle of קרא (H7121) 'calling/inviting.' The consonants are identical.

verses.literal: And he said to the one who called him when you make a meal of morning or a meal of evening do not desire to invite your lovers and not the brothers and not the relatives and not the wealthy neighbors for perhaps them that you [are] calling that they repay to you recompense.

verses.translation: But when you make an invitation call the poor and the disabled and the blind.
words: and the disabled / crippled (from נטל, carried away / removed)

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 as an adversative conjunction 'but/rather' — it contrasts with the previous instruction about who NOT to invite.
קרא (consonants קרא): Candidates: H7121 'to call out/address by name', H7122 'to encounter', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 'call/summon' — the imperative to invite guests.
textual_notes: והנטולים: No Strong's candidates were provided. The root נטל can mean 'to lift/carry' or 'to be taken away' — suggesting those whose limbs have been taken from them (i.e., the crippled/maimed). This is post-biblical Hebrew vocabulary.

verses.literal: But when you make an invitation call the poor and the disabled and the blind.

verses.translation: And blessed you will be for there is not to them what they will repay you and the reward you will attain it in the resurrection of the righteous.
words: they will repay you (from גמל + 2ms suffix)
you will attain it (hiphil of נשג/השיג)
in the resurrection of (noun from חיה)

translation_notes: וברוך: The candidate H1263 is the proper name Baruk. However, the consonants ברוך are the standard passive participle of ברך (H1288) meaning 'blessed.' The sentence 'and blessed you will be' is coherent; the proper name is not.
אין (consonants אין): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'there is not to them' = they do not have.

והשכר (consonants שכר): Candidates: H7936 'to hire', H7937 'to become tipsy', H7938 'wages', H7939 'payment/salary/compensation', H7941 'intoxicant'. Chose H7939 'reward/payment' — the noun with definite article, referring to divine recompense.
<יגמלוך: The damaged letter is likely ש, yielding שיגמלוך 'that they will repay you' (from גמל H1580). This continues the theme from section 2 about reciprocal repayment.
textual_notes: בתחיית: This noun form (תחייה) from the root חיה does not have a direct Strong's entry as a noun. It is a post-biblical Hebrew formation meaning 'resurrection/revival.' The concept 'resurrection of the righteous' is clear from context.
<יגמלוך: The damaged first letter is most likely ש (yielding שיגמלוך, 'that they will repay you'), though it could theoretically be another letter.

verses.literal: And blessed you will be for there is not to them what they will repay you and the reward you will attain it in the resurrection of the righteous.

verses.translation: And when one of his disciples heard these the words he said to him happy will be whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of YHWH.
words: happy / blessed (from אשר, with damaged letter)
that will eat (ש + יאכל from אכל)

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. Chose H834 — with prefix כ it forms כאשר 'when/as,' a temporal conjunction.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 'one' — 'one of his disciples.'
שמע (consonants שמע): Candidates: H8085 'to hear', H8087-8090 proper names/nouns. Chose H8085 — 'heard' as the completed action verb.

אלה (consonants אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H426 'God'. None of these match. The demonstrative pronoun אלה 'these' (H428) shares these consonants and fits perfectly: 'these words.'
אמר: Chose H559 'to say' — speech introduction verb.
מאו<ר: The damaged letter suggests מאושר 'happy/blessed' (from the root אשר H833/H835). The ש is the missing letter. This exclamation 'blessed/happy will be...' fits the context.
פת (consonants פת): Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel (of bread)', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 — eating bread/a morsel in the kingdom makes perfect sense.
מי (consonants מי): Only candidate H4310 'who/whoever'. Fits as the indefinite 'whoever will eat.'
textual_notes: אלה: The provided candidates do not include the demonstrative pronoun אלה (H428, 'these'), but the consonants are identical and the context ('these words') demands it. The candidates listed (bewail, adjure, oak, God) do not fit.

מאו<ר: With the damaged letter, this most likely reads מאושר (blessed/happy). The אשר root (H833/H835) supports this. An alternative reading מאור (H3974, 'light/luminary') is possible if the damaged letter is different, but 'happy/blessed will be' fits the exclamatory context better.

verses.literal: And when one of his disciples heard these the words he said to him happy will be whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of YHWH.

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to him a man one made an invitation great and invited men many.

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam (name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 — 'a man/person,' the subject of the parable.
אחד: Chose H259 'one' — used idiomatically as 'a certain [man].'
אמר: Chose H559 'to say.'
ישוע: Candidates H3442/H3443 both refer to Jeshua/Yeshua. Chose H3442.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said to him a man one made an invitation great and invited men many.

verses.translation: And he sent his servant at the time of the eating to call to the called-ones that they should come for already the all [is] prepared.
words: his servant (from שרת, to minister + 3ms suffix)
to the called ones / the invited

translation_notes: ושלח (consonants שלח): Candidates: H7971 'to send away/out', H7973 'a spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach (name)'. Chose H7971 — 'he sent' his servant.

translation_notes: המלח (h-m-l-ḥ): Candidates: H4414 'to pulverize/salt', H4415 'to eat salt', H4416 'salt', H4417 'powder/salt', H4418 'rag', H4419 'sailor', H3892 'fresh', H3893 'vigor'. In a statement about seasoning and taste, 'the salt' (H4417 with definite article) is the clear reading.
הוא (h-w-ʾ): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. As a pronoun in a nominal clause 'the salt it [is] good,' the pronoun H1931 fits.
טוב (ṭ-w-b): Candidates: H2895 'to be good (verb)', H2896 'good (adjective)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness (noun)'. As predicate adjective in a nominal clause, H2896 is correct.

אבל (ʾ-b-l): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'but/yet/truly'. As a conjunction introducing a contrast ('good, but if...'), H61 is the clear choice.
אם (ʾ-m): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Introducing a conditional clause about salt losing flavor, 'if' (H518) is the obvious reading.
במה (b-m-h): Candidates: H1116 'elevation/high place', H1117 'Bamah', H4100 'what?/how?'. As an interrogative 'with what will the taste be given?' — ב + מה (H4100) is the coherent reading.

הטעם (h-ṭ-ʿ-m): Candidates: H2938 'to taste (verb)', H2939 'to feed', H2940 'taste/perception', H2941 'sentence (Aramaic)', H2942 'flavor/judgment'. As a noun with definite article — 'the taste/flavor' — H2940 fits best.
textual_notes: ריקנית is a later Hebrew (Mishnaic) adjective meaning 'empty/void,' from the root ריק. It has no Strong's number. In context it describes salt that has become empty of its saltiness/potency — i.e., tasteless or impotent.

ינתן appears to be a niphal imperfect of נתן (to give), meaning 'will be given/restored.' The question is whether הטעם (the taste) is the subject ('how will the flavor be restored?') or the object. Niphal suggests the taste is the subject being passively restored.

verses.literal: The salt it [is] good but if the salt [becomes] empty in what will be given the taste

verses.translation: Not in the dust and not in the dung and not in [any] thing of benefit only it will be thrown outside who that has to him ears to hear let him hear

translation_notes: בעפר (b-ʿ-p-r): Candidates: H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher (name)', H6082 'fawn', H6083 'dust/earth/soil'. In context of agricultural uselessness (paired with dung/manure), 'soil/earth' (H6083) is the coherent reading — tasteless salt is useless even for the soil.

בזבל (b-z-b-l): Candidates: H2082 'to reside/dwell', H2083 'Zebul (name)'. Neither Strong's entry directly means 'dung/manure,' but the root זבל in post-biblical Hebrew means 'dung/manure' (cf. Mishnaic Hebrew זבל). In context paired with soil, this agricultural meaning is clearly intended — the salt is useless even as fertilizer.

בדבר (b-d-b-r): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. As a noun meaning 'thing/matter' — 'not in any useful thing' — H1697 is the natural reading.
רק (r-q): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. As an adverb limiting the outcome to being cast outside, 'only' (H7535) fits.

שיש (sh-y-sh): Candidates: H7893 'marble/white', H3426 'there is/exists'. Parsed as ש (relative particle) + יש (there is/has), meaning 'who has,' this is the coherent reading in context of 'whoever has ears.' Chose H3426.
ישולח: This appears to be a pual imperfect of שלח (to send/cast), meaning 'it will be thrown/cast out.' No Strong's candidate was provided but the root is שלח (H7971).
textual_notes: בזבל: The Strong's candidates (H2082 'to reside', H2083 'Zebul') do not capture the post-biblical meaning 'dung/manure' that is clearly intended here by context (soil and manure as agricultural uses for salt).
תועלתי is a later Hebrew form meaning 'beneficial/useful,' from the root יעל (to profit/benefit). It has no Strong's number.
The brackets ] [ at the end likely indicate a lacuna or scribal notation in the manuscript.
ישולח could be parsed as pual (passive intensive) of שלח, or as a later Hebrew form. The passive sense 'it will be cast/thrown' fits the context of discarding useless salt.

verses.literal: Not in the dust and not in the dung and not in [any] thing of benefit only it will be thrown outside who that has to him ears to hear let him hear
